findings: Public Road inventory contains no tariff objects.
E-Flux official documentation confirms charging tariffs are set by individual charge-point owners/operators and can be static or dynamic.
The public E-Flux app exposes pricing UI and contains map/tariff models.
Unauthenticated GET requests to map/search routes are not available.
The app binary contains Firebase App Check handling and authenticated session lifecycle code.
No attempt is made to bypass JWT authentication, Firebase App Check, or device/app attestation.
nextSafeRoutes: Use an official public tariff feed if Road exposes one later.
Use owner/operator first-party public pricing where a station-exact tariff is published.
If the user supplies an authorized API/app session intended for this use, re-evaluate within that authorization.
notes: 8045/8174 EVSEs use BE*EFL; the remaining 129 are the compact equivalent BEEFLEV... and belong to the same Road/E-Flux family.
No generic price is inferred for any Road EVSE.
